title: Unrestrained Simplex Denoising for Discrete Data. A Generative Method Applied to Graphs.
claim: Linear-interpolant noising causes abrupt jumps and stays within original class regions, whereas a parametric probability path evolves smoothly across the simplex.
layout: 2 rows by 5 columns, left-to-right time steps, rows contrast noising schemes
description: Two rows of five triangle plots, each showing the 3-class probability simplex with Voronoi region boundaries drawn inside. Columns are labeled t = 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25 and 0 from left to right. Points are colored yellow, purple and crimson by their original vertex. In the top row (linear interpolant), points sit exactly at the vertices at t = 1, then form sharp clusters that stay inside their own Voronoi regions up to t = 0.5, and then abruptly mix by t = 0.25 and t = 0. In the bottom row (parametric probability path), points start as soft clusters near the vertices and spread gradually and continuously toward a uniform mix at t = 0, with no jump. The eye goes first to the colored point clouds in the triangles.
caption: Upper row: Noising with a linear interpolant creates discontinuities and, for t > 0.5, all points remain in the Voronoi region of their original vertex. Lower row: Noising with an explicit parametric probability path avoids discontinuities.
abstract: Denoising models such as Diffusion or Flow Matching have recently advanced generative modeling for discrete structures, yet most approaches operate directly in the discrete state space, leading to abrupt state changes. We introduce simplex denoising, a simple yet effective generative framework that operates on the probability simplex. The key idea is a non-Markovian noising scheme in which, for a given clean data point, noisy representations at different times are conditionally independent. While preserving the theoretical guarantees of denoising-based generative models, our method removes unnecessary constraints, thereby improving performance and simplifying the formulation. Empirically, \emph{unrestrained simplex denoising} surpasses strong discrete diffusion and flow-matching baselines across synthetic and real-world graph benchmarks.
